newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING gets Canadian phone banking licence.
newsitem.headline: ING gets Canadian phone banking licence.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said on Monday it had received government approval to offer telephone banking services in Canada.
"We received a licence from the (Canadian) Ministry of Finance last week," ING spokeswoman Manel Vrijenhoek told Reuters.
She said ING now needed a licence from the provincial government in Ontaria, where its new trust company, ING Direct, would start direct marketing of banking services.
"We expect that within about 10 days. But that's a simpler procedure than getting the federal licence," she added.

ING executive board chairman Add Jacobs said last month that ING Direct would be a pilot project for similar initiatives by the Dutch group in the United States and other countries with mature financial services industries.
It has earmarked an initial investment of $50 million to start ING Direct, which will begin in Toronto with about 100 staff, offering savings and loans products.
It is ING's first move into banking in Canada, where it has operated insurance businesses under other names for 40 years.
